doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: His parents at gigs and the bad substitute drummer at Hobart
summary: His father played piano to age 95, and his parents drove to Geneva but left because the substitute drummer was too poor to be the band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I’ve had a number of musicians say that. Yeah, that that was a big transition from swing to straight-eighth notes is how some of the musicians would characterize it. That’s terrific. And your parents thought this was a pretty good way for you to make a buck?

They not only, of course my dad loved music so much that he was happiest when he was either playing or listening. I mean this guy played until he was 97 and he just finally just ran out of steam. In fact the last time I played with my dad we were playing and I was thinking you know, this guy on piano, his time is rock solid and his harmonies were just delicious and then all of a sudden I’d think wait a minute, that’s my dad, he’s 97. But he was 95 then I shouldn’t exaggerate. He was 95. But every once in a while we’d be playing a gig and you’d look out and there were mother and dad, they had their drink in their hand and they were right there cheering the band on and they would drive up to these things just to listen. And people were always very nice to them, they’d always get them drinks and they had a good time.
That’s a great feeling. I had a similar circumstance when I was actually in my rock & roll days, my parents would come out and support the band even though it probably wasn’t their cup of tea.

In fact there’s a funny story about that that sort of goes along with the other stuff we were talking about, that as I said we always had these spectacular drummers except one night all three of them couldn’t make it. We had a gig at Hobart. And so they suggested this other high school kid. So I mean we were so spoiled by Ronny Zito and Jimmy Wormworth and Grogan that we were just wow, this guy’s probably just as good. Well we got out there and he was just dreadful, he was awful. And I felt badly for him because he was a young child and he just was out of his element. But the band just sounded awful. So as it turned out my folks had driven all the way from Albany to Geneva New York, which is a pretty good hike, to hear the band. They walked up and down listening for the band and when they heard this they said, “That can’t be the Catatonic Five because they always have good drummers. So they went home which was just as good because we didn’t play well that night.
I’ll be darned, they never even found you, they just said no that wasn’t us.
They said that wasn’t us if they have a drummer like that.
